st: Melt the butter in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for [[10 minutes]] until soft and golden. Move to a bowl.
Warm the sauerkraut in a small pan over low heat for 5 minutes.
Put the sausages in the skillet with [[1 cup]] beer or water. Bring to a simmer and cook covered, turning once.
Pour off the liquid and let the sausages brown in the pan over medium-high heat, turning often until deep golden.
Check that the sausages reach 160°F (71°C) in the center.
Split the rolls, spread with mustard, and tuck in a sausage.
Top with the onions and sauerkraut and serve hot.
Place each cutlet between sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a mallet or heavy pan to 0.25 inch thick.
Season both sides with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Set out three plates: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs. Dip each cutlet in flour and shake off the excess, then the egg, then press into crumbs. Do not press crumbs too hard.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil and [[4 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until the butter foams.
Fry one or two cutlets at a time, shaking the pan gently so the hot fat puffs the crumb coat.
Cook about [[2 minutes]] per side until golden brown. Pork cutlets must reach 145°F (63°C).
Drain on paper towels and serve right away with lemon wedges and potato salad.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for [[4 minutes]] until soft.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] curry powder, the paprika and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the ketchup, [[0.5 cup]] water, vinegar, brown sugar and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Blend the sauce smooth with a blender or immersion blender if you prefer.
Cook the sausages in a skillet over medium heat, turning, until browned and they reach 160°F (71°C).
Cut the sausages into thick slices on a plate.
Pour the warm sauce over and dust with a little curry powder. Serve with fries or a roll.
Bring the vinegar, water, half the onions and carrots, the bay leaves, cloves, peppercorns, sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt to a boil. Cool completely.
Place the beef in a deep non-metal container and pour in the cooled marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 days, turning daily.
Remove the beef, pat dry, and strain the marinade, saving the liquid and vegetables.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef on all sides. Rub with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add the marinade vegetables and about [[2 cups]] of the marinade. Cover and simmer on low heat until the beef is very tender.
Take out the beef and rest under foil. Strain the liquid, add the raisins and the crushed gingersnaps and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Slice the beef and serve with the sweet-sour gravy, red cabbage and potato dumplings.
Lay the beef slices flat. Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper, then spread each with [[1.5 tsp]] mustard.
Top each slice with a bacon slice, some onion and half a pickle.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Secure each roll with toothpicks or kitchen twine.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the rolls on all sides.
Add the remaining onion and cook 3 minutes. Pour in the wine and [[1.5 cups]] broth and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer on low heat until the beef is fork-tender.
Take out the rolls. Stir [[2 tbsp]] flour with a little water, whisk into the pan juices, and simmer 5 minutes into gravy.
Remove the picks, return the rolls to the gravy, and serve with potatoes or spaetzle.
Dry the pork knuckles very well. Score the skin in a diamond pattern with a sharp knife, cutting only through the skin.
Rub with [[1 tbsp]] coarse salt, the pepper, [[2 tsp]] caraway and the garlic. Let sit 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Place the onions, carrots and bay leaves in a roasting pan and add [[1 cup]] beer.
Set the knuckles on top and roast, basting with the pan juices occasionally, for 2 hours.
Raise the heat to 450°F (230°C), baste with [[1 cup]] more beer and roast until the skin puffs and turns crisp, watching closely.
Check that the meat is tender and reaches at least 190°F (88°C). Rest for 10 minutes.
Strain the pan juices for gravy and serve the knuckle with sauerkraut and dumplings.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, [[1 tsp]] salt and the nutmeg into a thick, elastic batter. Beat until bubbles form, then rest 15 minutes.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and cook the onions over medium heat until deep golden brown and sweet.
Boil a large pot of water with [[1 tsp]] salt. Press the batter through a spaetzle maker or a large-holed colander straight into the water.
Cook each batch for [[2 minutes]] until the noodles float, then lift out with a slotted spoon.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Layer the noodles and cheese in a baking dish, ending with cheese.
Dot with [[2 tbsp]] butter and bake until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with the fried onions, pepper and chives and serve hot.
Boil the potatoes whole in salted water until tender when pierced.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp, then set aside on paper towels.
Drain the potatoes, let cool just enough to handle, peel and slice into thin rounds into a large bowl.
Whisk the warm broth, [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, [[3 tbsp]] oil, mustard, sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the warm potatoes and fold gently so they soak it up.
Add the onion, pickles and [[2 tbsp]] pickle brine and let sit for 30 minutes.
Fold in the bacon and chives, taste for salt and vinegar, and serve at room temperature.
Grate the potatoes and onion on the large holes of a box grater into a bowl.
Squeeze out all the liquid in a clean towel. Let the liquid stand 2 minutes, pour off the water, and add the starch at the bottom back to the potatoes.
Stir in the eggs, [[0.25 cup]] flour, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop in [[0.25 cup]] scoops of the mixture and flatten into thin rounds.
Fry [[4 minutes]] per side until crisp and golden brown, adding oil as needed.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with applesauce.
Remove the outer leaves from the cabbage, quarter it, cut out the core and slice the cabbage into very thin shreds.
Put the cabbage in a big bowl with [[1.5 tbsp]] salt and mix. Massage and squeeze with your hands for [[8 minutes]] until it gets wet and limp.
Mix in the caraway, onion and juniper.
Pack the cabbage firmly into a clean wide jar, pressing down so the brine rises above the cabbage.
Weigh the cabbage down with a small jar of water or a fermenting weight so it stays under the brine. Cover loosely with a cloth.
Leave at cool room temperature for 7 days, pressing down daily and skimming off any scum. Taste after day 5.
When tangy enough, seal and store in the refrigerator. Serve cold or warmed with sausages.
Mix the warm water, yeast and sugar and let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Stir in the flour, fine salt and butter. Knead for [[8 minutes]] until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a 24-inch rope, thicker in the middle. Twist into a pretzel shape.
Bring [[8 cups]] water to a boil and carefully add [[0.33 cup]] baking soda (it will foam). Boil each pretzel for 30 seconds per side.
Place on the sheets, sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] coarse salt and bake until deep brown.
Cool on a rack for 10 minutes before serving.

ing: optional; use cherry juice for no alcohol
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9-inch springform pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Beat the yolks with [[0.5 cup]] sugar for 5 minutes until pale and thick. Whisk in the vanilla.
Sift the flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt together, then fold into the yolk mixture.
Beat the whites to soft peaks, add [[0.5 cup]] sugar and beat to stiff peaks. Fold into the batter in three parts.
Pour into the pan and bake until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely. Cut the cake into 3 layers.
Simmer [[1 cup]] cherry juice with the cornstarch until thick, add the cherries and cool. Brush layers with kirsch or juice.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar until stiff. Layer cake, cherries and cream, cover the outside with cream, and press chocolate shavings on top.

ing: peeled and thinly sliced, like Granny Smith
st: Mix the flour, salt, egg, [[3 tbsp]] oil and [[0.5 cup]] warm water. Knead for [[10 minutes]] until smooth and soft. Coat in oil, cover and rest 45 minutes.
Toast the breadcrumbs in [[2 tbsp]] butter until golden. Toss the apples with the sugar, cinnamon, raisins and lemon juice.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Stretch the dough on a floured cloth, pulling it with the backs of your hands until paper-thin and about 20x30 inches.
Brush with [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and sprinkle the crumbs over the bottom third. Spread the apples over the crumbs.
Fold in the sides and roll it up using the cloth to lift. Place seam side down on a lined tray, curving slightly if needed.
Brush with [[2 tbsp]] butter and bake until deep golden and crisp.
Cool 15 minutes, dust with the powdered sugar and slice. Serve warm.
Set the cheese and butter out 20 minutes before serving. Brotzeit is a casual meal so nothing needs to be perfect, only fresh and plentiful.
Slice the Landjäger on a slant and the Leberkäse into pieces about 1/4 inch thick. Warm the Leberkäse in a pan for a few minutes if you like, but it is also good cold.
Fold the Bergkäse slices in half and fan them out along the board. Spoon the Obatzda into a small bowl and swirl the top with a spoon.
Wash the radishes, trim the tops and slice them thin. Salt them lightly just before serving so they stay crisp. Scatter the onion rings over the Obatzda.
Slice the rye bread and stack the pretzels in a corner. Put [[4 tbsp]] butter in a small dish with a knife.
Set the gherkins and [[3 tbsp]] mustard in small bowls and fill the board gaps with radish slices. Serve with cold beer.
nt: No cook: slice, fold, arrange; cheeses at room temperature 20 minutes
Best swap: Camembert mashed with butter, paprika and onion for homemade Obatzda; vegetarians drop the sausage and add extra cheeses and a boiled egg.

st: Pour the hot water over [[2 cup]] rye meal in a bowl. Stir, cover and soak for 8 hours or overnight until the grains swell and soften.
Mix in the rye flour, remaining [[1 cup]] rye meal, starter, [[1 tbsp]] molasses and [[2 tsp]] salt. The dough will be very wet and heavy like thick mud.
Grease a lidded loaf pan or cover a regular loaf pan tightly with foil. Press the dough in firmly with wet hands and smooth the top.
Heat the oven to 250°F. Set the covered pan inside a deep roasting pan and pour in hot water halfway up the sides for a gentle steam bath.
Bake for 6 hours, topping up the hot water now and then. The loaf turns very dark brown and smells malty and sweet.
Turn it out and wrap in a damp cloth. Rest a full day before slicing as thinly as possible.
nt: Best swap: use cracked rye or whole rye berries pulsed in a blender if you cannot find rye meal.

ing: or cinnamon, clove, nutmeg, allspice mix
st: Heat the oven to 325°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment; place wafers on it if using.
Beat 3 eggs with [[0.75 cup]] brown sugar and [[2 tbsp]] honey for 4 minutes until thick and pale.
Stir together [[1.5 cups]] almonds, [[1 cup]] hazelnuts, [[0.25 cup]] flour, [[0.5 tsp]] baking powder, [[2 tsp]] spice and [[0.5 cup]] orange peel.
Fold the dry mix into the egg mixture until a thick, sticky batter forms.
Spoon about 2 tablespoons onto each wafer, or form rounds of 3 inches on parchment, smoothing the tops with a wet spoon.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes; the tops should feel just firm and stay pale. Cool fully on a rack.
Melt [[4 oz]] dark chocolate gently in a bowl over simmering water and brush it over the tops. Let set 30 minutes.
nt: Best swap: all ground almonds in place of the hazelnuts 1:1, and a glaze of 1 cup powdered sugar with 2 tbsp lemon juice instead of chocolate.

st: Warm [[0.5 cup]] of the milk to lukewarm, stir in the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] sugar, and leave 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[0.25 cup]] butter, one egg and the yeast mixture into a soft dough. Knead 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled. Press it into a greased 9 by 13 inch pan.
Melt [[0.25 cup]] butter with [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[2 tbsp]] milk, boil 2 minutes, then stir in the almonds and spread over the dough.
Bake at 375°F for 25 minutes until the topping is deep golden. Cool fully, then slice the cake in half horizontally.
Cook the pudding mix with [[1 cup]] milk and the remaining sugar until thick, cool with plastic on the surface, then fold in the whipped cream.
Spread the cream on the bottom layer, set the almond layer on top, and chill for 1 hour before cutting.
nt: Yeast dough baked at 375°F, no-bake cream
Best swap: use plant milk and vegan butter 1 to 1 in the dough and topping.

st: Mix the flour, 2 eggs, [[1 tbsp]] oil, a pinch of salt and [[3 tbsp]] water into a firm dough. Knead 6 minutes, wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Cook the onion in the butter over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft. Cool, then mix with pork, ham, chopped spinach, bread, remaining egg, parsley, nutmeg and salt.
Roll the dough into a thin rectangle, about 1/16 inch. Cut into strips about 4 inches wide.
Spread the filling along one half of each strip in a thin layer, leaving a 1/2 inch border. Fold over, press the edges, and cut into 3 inch squares. Press the edges with a fork to seal.
Bring the broth to a gentle simmer. Add the Maultaschen in batches and poach for 12 minutes, until the pork reaches 160°F and they float.
Ladle into bowls with broth and top with chives or crisp fried onions.
nt: Best swap: for a classic next-day version, slice leftover Maultaschen and pan-fry in butter with eggs. Use plant ground beef for a vegetarian filling.
